hints: The Poisson mean $45.2$ is large, so the Poisson probabilities are awkward to add up. A large-mean Poisson is approximated by a normal distribution that keeps the mean and has its variance equal to the mean too: $\text{N}(\ldots, \ldots)$.

Poisson is discrete and normal is continuous, so apply a continuity correction. 'More than 60' means $X \geqslant 61$, so the boundary on the continuous scale is half a unit below $61$. Standardise it: $z = \dfrac{\text{boundary} - 45.2}{\sqrt{45.2}}$.
You want the **upper** tail ('more than'), so the probability you need is $1 - \Phi(z)$.
Find $\Phi(z)$ with a table or the calculator's normal cdf, then subtract it from 1. Expect a small probability (the mean is $45.2$ and $60$ is well above it). Give 3 s.f.
walkthrough:
**Why use an approximation**

We want $\text{P}(X > 60)$ where $X \sim \text{Po}(45.2)$. Working that out exactly would mean adding up the probabilities for $61, 62, 63, \ldots$ for ever (or using $1 - \text{P}(X \leqslant 60)$ with 61 terms). For a Poisson with a large mean (a mean over about 15), the shape is very close to a bell curve, so we use a normal distribution instead.

**Choose the normal distribution (B1)**

For a Poisson variable the mean and the variance are equal. So the normal approximation takes mean $= 45.2$ and variance $= 45.2$.

$$X \approx Y \sim \text{N}(45.2,\ 45.2)$$

Take care: the second number is the variance, so the standard deviation is $\sqrt{45.2}$.

**Continuity correction**

$X$ only takes whole numbers; $Y$ takes any value. 'More than 60 enquiries' means $X = 61, 62, 63, \ldots$, i.e. $X \geqslant 61$. On a continuous scale the value 61 occupies the interval from $60.5$ to $61.5$. So 'at least 61' starts at $60.5$.

$$\text{P}(X > 60) = \text{P}(X \geqslant 61) \approx \text{P}(Y > 60.5)$$

**Standardise (first M1)**

$$z = \frac{60.5 - 45.2}{\sqrt{45.2}}$$$$60.5 - 45.2 = 15.3 \qquad \sqrt{45.2} = 6.7231$$$$z = \frac{15.3}{6.7231} = 2.276$$

The scheme still gives the method mark if the continuity correction is wrong or missing, but then the answer will not be exact enough, so do include it.

**Use the upper tail (second M1)**

The table or calculator gives the area to the **left** of $z$, $\Phi(z)$. We want the area to the **right**, so subtract from 1.

$$\text{P}(Y > 60.5) = 1 - \Phi(2.276)$$

$\Phi(2.276)$: normal table or calculator normal cdf $\to 0.98857$.

$$1 - 0.98857 = 0.01143$$

Quick check: $z$ above 2 means we are in the far right tail, so about 1% is sensible.

**Final answer**

The probability that the desk cannot deal with all the enquiries is $0.0114$ (3 s.f.).
